title: Coupled-Layer Codes: Beyond Quantum Product Constructions
authors: Shuyu Zhang, Tzu-Chieh Wei, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn
abstract: Product codes are an important class of quantum error-correcting codes constructed from multiple input codes, which can give rise to asymptotically good quantum low-density parity check codes. In previous work, we showed how the product between two codes can be physically implemented by coupling layers of the first code using checks of the second code. In this work, we further unify product code constructions with coupled-layer constructions of phases of matter by introducing coupled-layer codes. The essential strategy is to condense general excitations created by Pauli operators among multiple decoupled layers of the first code. The condensation is specified by an excitation algebra, which encodes the excitations, along with an algebra-preserving map. This coupling between layers generalizes the notion of gauging in physics as well as the mapping cone in homological algebra, and can be used to produce non-CSS codes. As examples, we show how coupled-layer codes reproduce the X-cube and Chamon models. We further generalize the balanced product code by allowing a unitary transformation in addition to a group action by free permutation and describe its corresponding coupled-layer construction. In particular, we show how balancing by a ZX-duality can reproduce non-CSS codes such as the fermionic toric code and the 3-fermion Walker-Wang model in 3D.
summary: This paper introduces 'coupled-layer codes' as a generalization of standard product constructions for building quantum error-correcting codes. By formalizing the coupling using excitation algebras and relating it to homological algebra concepts like mapping cones, the authors demonstrate how to generate non-CSS stabilizer codes. This advances the theoretical understanding of topological quantum computation by providing new methods to construct robust quantum codes.
main_problem: To generalize quantum product constructions for building quantum error-correcting codes beyond standard CSS settings by introducing 'coupled-layer codes.'
main_result: The coupled-layer construction provides a general framework to derive non-CSS stabilizer codes, reproducing models like the fermionic toric code and generalizing tensor products via mapping cone structures.
method: The method involves defining an excitation algebra and using an algebra-preserving map to condense Pauli excitations across multiple layers, relating the construction to homological concepts like the mapping cone.
model_or_system: The work focuses on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs), specifically building upon product codes by coupling layers of stabilizer codes. The underlying mathematical structure involves chain complexes and gauging symmetries.
key_observables: The resulting quantum error-correcting codes; the ability to produce non-CSS codes; commutation relations between various Pauli operators ($	ext{A}_p^{	ext{q}1}, 	ilde{f}	ext{q}$, etc.).
important_parameters: The structure of the underlying group $G$ and the specific coupling terms derived from the input CSS codes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on algebraic manipulations concerning overlaps between supports of Pauli operators, assuming certain commutation relations hold for simplification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the tensor product complex structure (Fig. 1), the general coupled-layer construction via gauging (Fig. 2 & 3), and the mathematical formalism using mapping cones to represent code products and surgeries (Fig. 4, 5, 6).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining product codes to introducing the generalized coupled-layer concept. It then details the connection to gauging symmetries and homological algebra via mapping cones, culminating in detailed algebraic proofs of commutation relations for the resulting operators.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful mathematical machinery (mapping cones, excitation algebras) to construct novel topological quantum codes that go beyond simple product constructions, which is crucial for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation.
